valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E on the ordinary share, converted to the NYSE ADR (SAN, USD). ADR ratio: 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share, per the deposit agreement exhibit to Santander Form 20-F (SEC, exhibit 2.2 to the FY2022 20-F: each ADS represents one of Banco Santander shares; depositary Citibank, N.A.). The ratio is therefore 1:1, applied as x1 to ordinary-share values. FX: EUR to USD at the ECB euro reference rate published 13 Nov 2026 14:10 CET by Banca di Italia, 1.1052 USD per EUR, held flat for all 12-month targets (no FX forecast). This is a 14:10 CET fixing, not the NYSE close. Earnings base: FY2026 underlying profit approximately EUR 14.98bn (9M 2026 underlying EUR 11.176bn plus a Q4 equal to Q3 underlying of EUR 3.8bn) over about 14.41bn shares, giving roughly EUR 1.04 per share (ADR-equivalent). FY2027 (calendar year, viewed at the Nov 2027 target date) is an operating assumption, not a sourced consensus. Dividends are excluded (price-only basis).

bear.driver: Earnings fall from FY26 with a weaker revenue path and higher credit or US retail drag; market refuses the premium multiple
bear.assumption: FY27 EPS EUR 0.95 (about -9% vs FY26 est.) at 9x = EUR 8.55 x 1.1052

base.driver: Mid-single-digit revenue growth and lower costs per Q3 2026 targets, with buybacks (about 15% of profit from 2027 policy) lifting per-share earnings about 10%; multiple near 11x for a profitable European bank with about 16% underlying RoTE
base.assumption: FY27 EPS EUR 1.15 (about +10% vs FY26 est.) at 11x = EUR 12.65 x 1.1052

bull.driver: RoTE trends toward the 20%+ ambition (stated for 2028) earlier than expected, with lower US retail losses and capital return above the 50% payout; multiple re-rates to 13x
bull.assumption: FY27 EPS EUR 1.30 (about +25% vs FY26 est.) at 13x = EUR 16.90 x 1.1052

valuation.implied_by_close: At the 13 Nov close of USD 12.21 (EUR 11.05 at 1.1052), the stock trades at about 10.6x FY26 est. EPS of EUR 1.04 and 9.6x base FY27 EPS of EUR 1.15. The median of the eight named analyst targets is EUR 13.50 (USD 15.09 at the event-date FX), which implies 11.7x base FY27 EPS, or EUR 1.23 of FY27 EPS at 11x (about 7% above the base EPS).
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E on base FY27 EPS moves the base target by USD 1.27, about 10.4 pp of the USD 12.21 close. FX is a translation effect only: each 0.01 move in USD per EUR moves the base target by about USD 0.13.
valuation.watch_metric: Underlying RoTE (16.0% in 9M 2026) holding at or above 16% while ordinary profit grows; cost-to-income falling as guided; CET1 staying in the 12.8-13% target range after the Webster acquisition (CET1 12.7% at 30 Sep 2026 after a 147 bp hit).
valuation.next_disclosure: FY2026 results (early February 2027; the FY2025 release was 3 Feb 2026, the 2027 date is not confirmed in the sources), and the Q1 2027 statement; FY2027 EPS and buyback pace appear there.

analyst_notes: Eight named analysts (Citi, RBC, Goldman Sachs and UBS Buy; JPMorgan and Jefferies Hold; Barclays and Morgan Stanley Buy) have dated calls from 2 Sep to 4 Nov 2026, with the cluster after the 28 Oct results. Named targets are EUR 12.90-15.00 (USD 14.46-17.02); their EUR median of 13.50 sits about 7% above the base-case EUR 12.65 (USD 13.98), so the gap is a higher FY27 earnings or multiple view. Horizons are not documented in the sources, so all target rows stay in the timeline with horizon null and are excluded from any weighted target. Barclays (21 Oct), JPMorgan (15 Oct) and Morgan Stanley (2 Sep) predate the 28 Oct results, and coverage is a partial panel.
